summary: Fafang (1904–1951) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Taixu and served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-Kuei Li (1902–1987) worked in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Tsinghua, Michigan (BA), Chicago (PhD under Edward Sapir), and Harvard, later teaching at Academia Sinica, Yale, Harvard, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and Hawaiʻi (1969–1974).
Faren works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Faren completed a PhD at Lancaster University by 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Farzand Ali Durrani (1933–2003) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of the Punjab, University of Peshawar (~1954–1958), and University of London (~1961–1964), and was a professor at the University of Peshawar (~1958–1993).

Fawad Khan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, serving as Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (attested 2022).

Fazun (1902–1980) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Taixu and at Drepung Monastery, directed the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies from 1933, and became vice president and president of the Buddhist Academy of China in 1956.

Ferdinand Christian Baur (1792–1860) worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen and Tübinger Stift (~1809–1814) and held a post at the University of Tübingen (~1826–1860).

Ferdinand Hitzig (1807–1875) was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. He studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829) and held posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi (1837–1907) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and completed his habilitation at Marburg (~1861), where he served as professor and later Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing (1882–1961) was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1905). He taught at Peking University (1919–1921), Humboldt University (~1925–1938), and UC Berkeley beginning in 1938.

Ferdinand Sommer (1875–1962) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen (1896) and completed his habilitation at Leipzig, subsequently holding professorships at Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure (1857–1913) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig University (1880) and taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1881–1891), the University of Paris (~1881–1891), and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).

Ferdinand von Eckstein (1790–1861) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer (~1810–1812), was a member of the Société Asiatique (~1822–1861), and founded Le Catholique in 1826.

Ferenc Ruzsa (born 1957) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982) and has served as a faculty staff member there since approximately 1989.
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University, where his doctoral supervisor was Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola (1915–2017) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the National University of San Marcos, was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (attested 1989), and directed the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (~1989–2017).
Filipp Fortunatov studied under Georg Curtius (~1871–1873) and Michel Bréal (~1872–1873).

Filippo Marsili is a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and held an academic post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

Finnian M. M. Gerety works in Indology and religious studies. After earning a doctorate from Harvard University by 2015 and completing a postdoc at Yale (2017–2018), he became a visiting assistant professor at Brown University (attested 2020).

Fitzedward Hall (1825–1901) was an Indologist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Sanskrit College and University before holding a chair at King's College London (1862) and serving as India Office librarian (~1862–1869).
